payload.context: The Treaty of Versailles was signed on 28 June 1919 and formally ended World War I between the Allied Powers and Germany. Its main provisions included: the War Guilt Clause (Article 231) assigning blame to Germany, substantial financial reparations later set at 132 billion gold marks, military restrictions limiting the German army to 100,000 troops and prohibiting an air force, and territorial losses including the return of Alsace-Lorraine to France and cession of territory to the new state of Poland.
